0.long_answer: Pseudocholinesterase deficiency is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. This means that an individual must inherit two mutant copies of the BCHE gene—one from each parent—in order to manifest the condition. Carriers, who have only one mutant copy, are typically asymptomatic because the presence of one normal gene copy is sufficient to produce enough enzyme activity. As a result, the disorder follows the classical pattern of autosomal recessive inheritance, where affected individuals are usually born to parents who are carriers of the mutation.
